source: Ministry of Agriculture training module "ជំនិតកម្មដំណាំខ្នុរសំរាប់កសិកម្ម" (Jackfruit Cultivation Techniques for Agriculture), prepared with participation from the Santisena organization, an elderly people's association, a charitable organization, and the CRS (Catholic Relief Services) agriculture program; content compiled with reference to fruit-tree materials and Prek Leap National School of Agriculture (សាលាជាតិកសិកម្មព្រែកលៀប).
text: Fertilizer should be applied twice a year, at the start and at the end of the rainy season. Dig small holes in a ring shape around the tree at a distance corresponding to the outer edge of the branch canopy (the dripline), then apply both natural (organic) fertilizer and a compound chemical fertilizer containing nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium (N-P-K). The diagram shows two figures pouring fertilizer into ring holes near the base of a tree, with measurements labeled approximately 0.4 and 0.5 meters, likely referring to the depth and/or distance of the fertilizing holes from the trunk — the exact assignment of which figure is depth versus distance was not fully legible in the scan.
